clue.text: Transport initially included in price of holiday

indicators.note: something included in another sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a fee is a price charged for a service

indicators.note: what comes initially is at the very start, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Getting to your destination costs extra on top of the holiday package price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Price of holiday' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits there: 'price' is the outer word and 'of' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is a festival or feast day, an older sense of holiday as a day of celebration.

clue.text: Piece of music at service primarily for common people

parts.note: a riff is a short repeated musical phrase
the Royal Air Force, one of the armed services

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the leading letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hymn or anthem chosen for a church service mainly for the benefit of ordinary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests church, but in crosswords it usually means one of the armed forces: RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Riff-raff is a disparaging term for the lowest classes, the rabble or hoi polloi.

clue.text: Closure of zoo interrupting bear's routine

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to bear something is to carry or bring it

indicators.note: a closure is an ending, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A zoo shutting down disrupts the daily habits of its bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning to carry, BRING. The 's stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine as an adjective means dull and unvaried, matching tedious or uninteresting.

clue.text: Setter ingesting ecstasy and heroin got nasty bug

indicators.note: to ingest is to take something inside, so one piece swallows the others

parts.note: Pan is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted or messed up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
H is slang for heroin
taken as written

explanation.surface: The crossword setter took drugs and came down with a horrible illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' means the person who wrote this puzzle, here Pan. The words 'and' and 'got' look like linking grammar, but 'got' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathogen is a microorganism that causes disease, which is what a bug means informally.

clue.text: End up having sleepover away from home

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word is read back to front

parts.note: the word splits as sleep, a nap, followed by the instruction over
someone who is not at home is out

explanation.surface: A night ends with someone staying over at a friend's place instead of going home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleepover' reads as one word, the childhood overnight stay, but it splits into 'sleep' and the instruction 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan out is to turn out or develop in a particular way, an idiom for how things eventually conclude.

clue.text: Covers for songs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: puts down over a surface, as a carpet or a table
second meaning: ballads or narrative poems meant to be sung

explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers for songs' suggests cover versions of tracks; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means spreads something over a surface, and the noun is an archaic term for short lyrical poems or ballads.

clue.text: Stone container with drug-free contents

indicators.note: contents are what sits inside a vessel, so these pieces go inside the other

parts.note: a pot is a container
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
to free something of a burden is to rid it

explanation.surface: A stone jar whose contents are guaranteed free of narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug-free' reads as a single adjective, but splits into a drug and a separate word for free.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gemstone, a variety of the mineral olivine.

clue.text: Vehicles crossing America in convoy

indicators.note: things crossing a land stretch across it, so the outer pieces span the inner one

parts.note: a car and a van are both vehicles
A is a standard abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A line of trucks drives together across the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'Vehicles' supplies two separate vehicles that sit either side of America's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a company of travellers journeying together, such as a train of camels or wagons.

clue.text: Letter following complaint?

parts.note: BEE is the spelled-out name of the second letter of the alphabet
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A letter written after somebody has grumbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like a position word, but here it supplies its own abbreviation F, as used in 'pp. 10f'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal slang for a grievance or grudge someone has against another.

clue.text: I soon chat freely, as part of a conspiracy

indicators.note: done freely means without fixed order, so these letters are rearranged at will

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone involved in a plot boasts that they will soon be talking openly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chat freely' reads like candid talk, but 'freely' tells you to rearrange the nine letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in cahoots is an idiom for colluding or scheming secretly together with others.

clue.text: Conservative bishop entertained by old artist

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: something old and no longer fresh is stale
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A right-wing churchman is hosted by an elderly painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old artist' reads as one phrase, but 'old' belongs to the wordplay and 'artist' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was an English Romantic painter known for landscapes such as The Hay Wain.

clue.text: Priest called to road accident

parts.note: P is an abbreviation for priest
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A clergyman is summoned to the scene of a car crash to give last rites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called to' sounds like being summoned, but 'called' is the past tense of phoning and 'to' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is British slang for a minor collision involving a car or aircraft.

clue.text: Philosopher climbing old mountain outside Turkish capital

indicators.note: pieces placed outside go around something, so they enclose the remaining letter
in a down entry climbing means going upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: a capital is an upper-case initial, so only the leading letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word
an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: A thinker ascends an ancient peak near Ankara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkish capital' points to Ankara, but 'capital' here means capital letter, the T at the start of Turkish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Greek thinker, student of Socrates and founder of the Academy in Athens.

clue.text: Bird near foot of mast on vessel

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: the foot of something is its bottom end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word
a jar is a vessel for holding things

explanation.surface: A seabird perches close to the base of a ship's mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'mast' suggest a ship, but the vessel here is a container. 'On' places the jar after the earlier pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal insect-eating bird with a distinctive churring call.

clue.text: Note found amongst burnt remains of US sect

indicators.note: something found amongst other things lies in their midst, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: ash is what is left after burning
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A message is discovered in the charred ruins of a religious group's compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests a written message, but here it is a musical note from do-re-mi.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a traditionalist Christian community in America known for shunning modern technology.

clue.text: Female supporter rejected as vulgar

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
a fan supports a team or performer

explanation.surface: A woman's admirer is spurned for being crude.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang, unfamiliar to many outside the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for tasteless, tacky or lacking in style.

clue.text: Limits of taboo stopping pleasure in bed

indicators.note: a stopper plugs the inside of a bottle, so one piece is lodged within another

parts.note: fun is pleasure or enjoyment

indicators.note: the limits of something are its edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Taboos put a brake on enjoyment between the sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pleasure in bed' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is the link and 'bed' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style padded mattress, often on a low frame, used for sleeping.

clue.text: Admirer and crook go to a dance

parts.note: a fan is an admirer

indicators.note: something crooked is bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fan and a criminal head off together to a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a noun for a criminal, but it acts as the signal to bend the preceding word.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish courtship dance performed in triple time with castanets.

clue.text: Ice originally put in china bucket

indicators.note: to put one thing in another is to place it inside, so one piece goes within

parts.note: china means mate, from Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' for mate, and a pal is a mate

indicators.note: what something was originally is how it began, so the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Ice cubes go into a porcelain bucket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like porcelain, but in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so china is a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is a container with a handle for carrying liquids, the same thing as a bucket.

clue.text: River stopping quiet monster's advance

indicators.note: a stopper plugs the inside of a bottle, so one piece is lodged within another

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
R is the abbreviation for river
an ogress is a female ogre, a monster

explanation.surface: A river halts the onward march of a silent beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monster's' looks possessive, but the 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition; the monster is a female ogre.
explanation.definitionFit: Progress means forward movement or headway, so as a noun it matches an advance.

clue.text: Hit cross back with handle

indicators.note: going back means going in the opposite direction, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: to bonk is to hit on the head
a rood is a crucifix or cross, especially in a church

explanation.surface: Someone angry strikes back with a weapon in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it is the noun rood, an old word for a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorknob is a round handle you turn to open a door.

clue.text: Radio broadcast by Elvis' first crew member?

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first means at the front, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A radio show featuring the debut of a member of Elvis Presley's team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suits a radio surface but is the signal to scatter letters. The question mark flags that crew here means a touring band's crew, not a ship's.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadie is a member of the touring staff who set up and move equipment for a band.

clue.text: Bamboo thatch covering market stall

indicators.note: a covering lies over something and conceals it, so the letters are concealed across the words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A trader's stall at the market has a roof of bamboo thatch.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the end of the first word and the start of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A booth is a small temporary structure from which goods are sold at a fair or market.

clue.text: Perfect hit to leg

parts.note: to bang is to hit hard
in cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A batter's flawless shot is played away toward the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the half of the field behind the batter's legs is called both leg side and on side, so leg gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang on is British informal for exactly right or spot on, the same as flawless.

clue.text: A male line broken in battle

indicators.note: a broken thing has its parts disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier's line of defence gives way during combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line broken in battle' paints a military scene, but 'broken' is the signal to rearrange the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: El Alamein in Egypt was the site of the decisive 1942 Second World War clash between Montgomery and Rommel.

clue.text: Censor woman with no husband

indicators.note: having no part of something means lacking it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Edith is a woman's name
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A single woman acts as a censor.
explanation.walkthrough: Any woman's name could fit; the missing H narrows it to one ending in that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To censor material is to edit it, cutting or altering parts considered unacceptable.

clue.text: Retired thespian ignoring head of casting's staffing schedule

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run the other way
to ignore something is to leave it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a thespian is an actor

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so only the leading letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A former actor disregards the casting director's work timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like a description of the thespian's career, but it is the signal to turn the word around. The 's is 'is', the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a list showing when each person in a team is due to work, a duty roster.

clue.text: Net found twisted round foot of body in river

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps another
something twisted is distorted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the foot of something is its bottom end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fishing net, wound around a corpse's foot, is discovered in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body in river' paints a grim discovery, but 'in' is only the link. The Tyne is the river through Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyne is a river in north-east England, flowing through Newcastle to the North Sea.

clue.text: Journalist finally in digs broadcast news

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order
finally means at the end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reporter at last reaches their lodgings and puts out the latest bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: Digs is British informal for rented lodgings. 'Broadcast news' sounds like a TV bulletin, but 'broadcast' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings is an old-fashioned word for news or information that has been received.

clue.text: Composer crossing heart on island

indicators.note: the heart is the core, so the edge letters are dropped and the middle is kept

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A musician crosses over with his heart set on reaching an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' looks like a container signal, but it is the word whose middle supplies most of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian opera writer behind The Barber of Seville and William Tell.
